subject.title: Feature: config-level default task notify policy

question: Should OpenClaw expose a public config-level default task notify policy, and should that config be a single global default or a per-runtime policy map?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but choosing the config contract changes defaults and channel delivery semantics for existing users, which automation should not decide without maintainer intent.

options.title: Per-runtime default map
options.body: Add a strict config surface such as agents.defaults.tasks.notifyPolicy with per-runtime entries so ACP/subagent can be changed without disturbing cron, CLI, and media defaults.

options.title: Single global default
options.body: Add one defaultNotifyPolicy with explicit code exceptions for runtimes that must remain silent, accepting a simpler user model but more special-case logic.

options.title: No new config surface
options.body: Keep per-task CLI overrides and address narrower Discord/Codex/ACP visibility issues individually instead of adding another global config knob.

recommendation.title: Per-runtime default map
recommendation.body: Add a strict config surface such as agents.defaults.tasks.notifyPolicy with per-runtime entries so ACP/subagent can be changed without disturbing cron, CLI, and media defaults.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent adjacent work touched requester attribution, task docs, and subagent delivery paths, making this the best available routing candidate for the public config/default decision.
